claims.behaviour: Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `export-format` `ms-excel` and one `column-key` `field`. Asked for any format other than `ExportFormat.MS_EXCEL` it returns null; asked for a column whose key is neither `field` nor `timeAggregate` it returns null (a `timeAggregate` column is handled like `field` when the provider is asked directly, although the descriptor only registers `field`).

The column parameter `field` (a single value; the first element when it is a list) names the Jira field. When it is missing or empty the provider throws `StructureProviderException` with message `field parameter is required`, so the column is skipped.

The field is looked up by exact id among the fields Jira's `FieldManager.getAvailableNavigableFields(user)` returns for the export context's user. That set is read once per export request context and reused for every column of the export; a `FieldException` while reading it is logged as a warning and treated as no fields. A field id that is not in the set (unknown, hidden or not navigable for the user) makes the provider return null.

The field's value is requested as an attribute built from the field id: `issuekey` becomes attribute `key`; `customfield_<n>` with a numeric n becomes attribute `customfield` with parameter `fieldId` = n (an integer); any other id (including `customfield_x` with a non-numeric suffix) is used as the attribute id. The format is `html`, with no further parameters in the Excel export.

Column parameter `aggregate`: absent means the field's own value. `sum` means the sub-tree sum: attribute `sum` (format `html`) with parameter `attribute` = the field's attribute (format `duration` when the field is one of Jira's time-tracking duration fields, an `AbstractDurationSystemField`, otherwise `number`) and parameter `distinct` = the column's boolean `distinct` (false when absent). Any other `aggregate` value throws `StructureProviderException` `aggregate type <value> is not supported` (column skipped). The typed cell rules below then read this `sum` attribute in the number, time or duration format they need.

Header text: the column's name when it is non-empty; otherwise the Jira field's name (its id when the name is empty). For an `aggregate`=`sum` column without a name the header is i18n `sw.column.opt.aggr.sum.colname` (`Σ {0}`) with the field's name, e.g. `Σ Time Spent`.

Every Excel field column ends with a rich-text rule: it requests the field's attribute in `html` format with the extra parameter `excel` = true and, when that value is non-null, sets it with `ExcelCell.setRichTextFromHtml`. Typed rules (below) come first; when their typed value is null the rich-text value is used; when that is null too the cell stays empty. Fields without a typed rule get only the rich text, with the column left in the `DEFAULT` style. (General rule for this group's renderers: a renderer requests, in `prepare`, every attribute any of its cell rules reads, whatever the export format; on `renderCell` it tries its cell rules in order and the first one that finds a non-null value sets the cell; if none does, the cell stays empty.)

For field `issuekey` the column's default style is `ExcelStyle.HYPERLINK_UNDECORATED` and the cell, when the attribute `key` (text) is non-empty, is `setHyperlink(key, url)` with attribute `url` (text) as the URL, or `setText(key)` when the URL is null. An empty or missing key falls back to the rich text.

A custom field is numeric when its type key is `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:float`, or its JSON schema type is `number` and it is neither an Agile rank field nor of type `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:importid`. Numeric fields and Agile rank fields (type keys `com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira:gh-global-rank`, `com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira:greenhopper-ranking`) get the header style `HEADER_RIGHT_ALIGNED` and the cell `setNumber` of the attribute read in `number` format.

A custom field whose type is a Jira `DateTimeCFType` gets column style `DATETIME`, a right-aligned header and `setDatetime(new Date(v))` with v the attribute read in `time` format (epoch ms). Otherwise, a custom field whose type implements Jira's `DateField` gets style `DATE`, a right-aligned header and `setDate(new Date(v))`. The date-time check comes first.

A custom field whose type is Jira's `URLCFType` gets column style `HYPERLINK` (the header keeps the left-aligned style). The cell reads the field's `html` value (without the `excel` parameter), trims it and, when it is non-empty and `new java.net.URL(value)` accepts it, sets `setHyperlink(value, value)`; otherwise (empty, malformed, or HTML markup) it falls back to the rich text.

A non-custom field implementing Jira's `DateField` (such as created, updated, due date, resolution date) gets column style `DATE`, a right-aligned header and `setDate` of the attribute in `time` format: only the date is exported, also for created and updated, which carry a time of day.

Jira's time-tracking duration fields (`AbstractDurationSystemField`: original estimate, remaining estimate, time spent and their aggregate forms) get column style `DURATION`, a right-aligned header and `setDuration(ms / 1000)` (integer division) of the attribute in `duration` format (milliseconds).

The votes and watches system fields (`VotesSystemField`, `WatchesSystemField`) get a right-aligned header and `setNumber` of the attribute in `number` format. For the thumbnail system field (`ThumbnailSystemField`) the provider returns null, so the column is not exported. Every other system field gets only the rich text.
Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `export-format` `ms-excel` and `column-key`s `joined` and `icons`. For any other format or column key it returns null.

The column's multi-value parameter `fields` lists Jira field ids. When it is missing or empty the provider throws `StructureProviderException` `fields parameter is required` (column skipped). Ids not among the user's available navigable fields (looked up as for `exportrenderer-excel-field`) are skipped silently; a field listed twice is used once, at its first position.

The provider does not return a renderer (it returns null). Instead it hands the exporter, through the export request context, a list of renderers, one per listed available field in list order, and the exporter exports each of them as a separate spreadsheet column in place of the joined (or icons) column. Each field column is rendered exactly as `exportrenderer-excel-field` renders a non-aggregated `field` column for that field (attribute in `html` format without parameters, same typed cells, styles and rich-text fallback). An `icons` column therefore exports the fields' values, not icons. When none of the listed fields is available the list is empty and the column counts as not handled.

The header of each split column ignores the joined column's own name: it is the i18n text of the field's Jira column heading key (`NavigableField.getColumnHeadingKey()`) with the field's name as argument {0}; when the heading key is empty it is the field's name (its id when the name is empty).
A listed thumbnail field produces no column: its slot in the list is empty, the exporter logs a warning for it and exports the other fields' columns normally.

Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `export-format` `printable` and `column-key` `field`. It returns null for any format other than `ExportFormat.PRINTABLE`. Column keys, the required `field` parameter and its error, the field lookup, the field-to-attribute mapping, `aggregate`=`sum` (and its error) and the header text are exactly as for `exportrenderer-excel-field`.

Every row's cell is `PrintableCell.setHtml` of the field's attribute in `html` format (for `sum`, the `sum` attribute in `html`); a null value leaves the cell empty. There are no typed cells: numbers, dates and durations appear as the attribute's HTML.

The column is multiline (`setMultiline(true)`) exactly when the requested attribute id is `issuelinks`, `labels`, `environment`, `description` or `customfield` (so every `customfield_<n>` field wraps); otherwise, including the issue key and every `sum` column, it is single-line.

For a user field (system fields `assignee`, `creator`, `reporter`, or a custom field whose JSON schema type is `user`) whose column parameters contain the key `view`, the value of `view` is passed unchanged as attribute parameter `view` (for a custom field next to `fieldId`). Other fields never get it, and `sum` columns do not pass it.

Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `export-format` `printable` and `column-key` `joined` (printable `icons` columns go to `exportrenderer-print-icons`). It returns null for other formats or keys. The `fields` parameter, its `fields parameter is required` error and the field lookup are as for `exportrenderer-excel-joined`; each available field is requested as its attribute in `html` format without parameters.

Header text: the column's name; when the name starts with `{` and ends with `}` the text between them is used as an i18n key and translated with the export context's i18n helper. When the name is null or empty the header is i18n `sw.column.type.joined` (`Multiple Fields`).

Each cell is one `setHtml` with the non-empty HTML values of the listed fields concatenated in list order with no separator; it is set even when every value is empty (an empty string), and no CSS class is added. The column is single-line.

Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `export-format` `printable` and `column-key` `icons`. It returns null unless the format is `ExportFormat.PRINTABLE` and the column key is `icons`.

Each id in the multi-value parameter `fields` maps to an icon attribute in `html` format: `issuetype` to `issuetype.icon`, `priority` to `priority.icon`, `status` to `status.icon`, `assignee` to `assignee.icon` with parameter `print` = true, `reporter` to `reporter.icon` with `print` = true, `project` to `project.icon`. Ids are kept in list order, a repeated id gives its icon twice.

A missing or empty `fields` throws `StructureProviderException` `fields parameter is required`; any id not in the six supported ones throws `field <id> is not supported`. Either way the whole column is skipped.

Header text: the column's name, or i18n `sw.column.type.icons` (`Icons`) when it is empty. Each cell is `setHtml` of the non-empty icon HTML values concatenated in order without separator (empty string when none) and gets the CSS class `s-icons`.
Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `main` and no export format, so it serves both formats. It returns null for any other column key.
Header text: the column's name when non-empty; otherwise the name of the Jira field `summary` (`FieldManager.getField("summary")`), or its id when that name is empty.

Cells show attribute `summary` (format `text`) with parameter `aggregate` = true. When the value is null (item missing, failed or not visible) the cell shows i18n `s.w.item-loading-failed` (`Unavailable item`) instead; the cell is never left empty.
In the printable export the column is multiline, its header cell gets CSS class `s-mn`, and each cell is `setText` (HTML-escaped by the cell) with CSS class `pad` added.

In the Excel export each cell is `setText` of the summary and `ExcelCell.setIndention(row depth)` (0 for top-level rows; the cell clamps it to 15). The column keeps the default style and left-aligned header.
Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `progress` and no export format (both formats). Returns null for other column keys.

It requests attribute `progress` (format `number`) with parameters `basedOn` (the column's single value, omitted when absent), `resolvedComplete` and `includeSelf` (booleans, false when absent), `weightBy` when the column has it, and `weightByField` only when both `weightBy` and `weightByField` are present.

Depending on `basedOn` it adds: `status` - `statuses` (list of strings) and `percents` (list of longs); `category` - `categories` (list of strings) and `categoryPercents` (list of longs); `percentfield` - `percentField` (single value). For other values (including absent) none of these. Other column parameters are not passed on.

Header text: the column's name, or i18n `s.columns.progress.name` (`Progress`). Excel: column style `PERCENTAGE`, header `HEADER_RIGHT_ALIGNED`. Printable: percentage style `PERCENT_TEXT` when the boolean column parameter `displayPercents` is true, else `PROGRESS_BAR`. Each cell is `setPercentage(value as double)` (a fraction, 1.0 = 100 %); null leaves it empty.
Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `worklogged` and no export format (both formats). Returns null for other column keys.

It requests attribute `worklogged` (format `duration`) with `timeZone` when the column has it, and at most one user filter: `author` when present, else `group` when present, else `role` when present (the others are dropped).

When the column's `period` is one of `today`, `this_week`, `this_month`, `this_year`, `yesterday`, `last_week`, `last_month`, `last_year`, it is passed as parameter `period`. Otherwise both `dateFrom` and `dateTo` must be present and are passed unchanged as parameters `dateFrom` and `dateTo` (no `period`); when either is missing the provider returns null and the column is not exported.

With `aggregate` = `sum` the attribute becomes `sum` (format `duration`) with `attribute` = the worklogged attribute and `distinct` = the column's boolean `distinct` (false when absent). Any other `aggregate` value is ignored (no sum, no error).

Header text: the column's name, otherwise i18n `sw.column.worklogged.period.+<period>+.colname` (with the literal plus signs), e.g. `Work Today`, `Work This Week`, `Work Last Month`, and for `date_range` `Work Logged`; for a sum column that text is wrapped in `sw.column.opt.aggr.sum.colname` (`Σ {0}`). A date-range column without a `period` value asks for the key with `null` in place of the period, which the bundle does not have (as the original does).
In both formats the column style is `DURATION` (Excel), the header right-aligned, and each cell `setDuration(ms / 1000)` of the attribute; null leaves the cell empty.
Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `attribute` and no export format (both formats). Returns null for other column keys.

The attribute comes from the column parameter `attribute`, an object with `id`, `format` and optional `params` (object). The `format` must be one of the standard `ValueFormat` ids (`html`, `text`, `id`, `number`, `boolean`, `time`, `duration`, `json`, `jsonArray`, `any`, `order`). When `attribute` is missing, not an object, has an unknown or missing format, or an invalid id or params, the provider throws `StructureProviderException` `invalid column spec: no attribute` (column skipped).
Header text: the column's name when non-empty, otherwise the attribute id.

When the attribute's format is `html`, or one the plugin converts to HTML (`text`, `number`, `duration`, `time`, `boolean`), the printable cell is `setHtml` of the attribute in `html` format and the Excel cell is rich text (`setRichTextFromHtml`) of the attribute in `html` format with extra parameter `excel` = true. For any other format (`id`, `json`, `jsonArray`, `any`, `order`) both formats get `setText` of the attribute requested in `text` format. Null values leave the cell empty.

Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `seq` and no export format (both formats); null for other keys. Header: the column's name, or i18n `sw.column.seq.title` (`Index`). Each cell is `setText` of attribute `seq` (format `text`, the row's outline number such as `1.2.3`); null leaves it empty. No styles.

Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `itemid` and no export format (both formats); null for other keys. Header: the column's name, or i18n `sw.column.type.itemid` (`Item ID`). It requests no attributes.

Each cell is `setText` of the row's item identity: for an issue the decimal issue id (e.g. `10001`); for any other item the identity text (`<type>/<long id>` or `<type>//<string id>`) with a leading `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-` removed, e.g. `folder/12`, `generator/3`; third-party type keys stay complete. It is set for every row, also rows the user cannot see.

Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `rowid` and no export format (both formats); null for other keys. Header: the column's name, or i18n `sw.column.type.rowid` (`Row ID`). Each cell is `setText` of the row's forest row id in decimal, for every row (no attributes are requested).

Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `formula` and no export format (both formats). It returns null for other column keys, and also when the column's `formula` parameter is missing or empty (the column is then not exported by it).

The display format is the column's object parameter `displayFormat`, or, when that is absent, the legacy object `numberFormat`. Its `type` selects the cell kind: `number`, `percentage`, `datetime`, `duration`, `wiki`; a missing display format, a missing type or any other type means plain text.

Without a sum the value is attribute `expr` with parameters `formula` (the column's formula unchanged) and `variables` (a copy of the column's `variables` object; an empty object when absent or not an object). For type `wiki` it is wrapped as attribute `wiki-render` (format `html`) with `attribute` = that `expr` in `text` format.

With `aggregate` = `sum` the formula is rewritten to `WITH summable = (<formula>): IF summable.IS_ARRAY(): SUM(summable) ELSE summable` (arrays are summed first) and the value is attribute `sum` with `attribute` = that `expr`, and `distinct` = the column's boolean `distinct`, both in format `duration` when the type is `duration` and `number` otherwise (also for `wiki`, which then shows the sum's HTML). For type `datetime` a warning `cannot export or calculate a sum of date/time values` is logged and the sum is exported anyway.

Header text: the column's name when non-empty; otherwise the formula trimmed and cut to its first 15 characters; when the trimmed formula is empty (whitespace only) i18n `s.w.formula.column-type.name` (`Formula`).

Type `number`: Excel column style `DEFAULT`, header right-aligned; when the display format has `rounding`, the column gets `setRounding(rounding clamped to 0..9)`. The value is read in `any` format: a `Number` is `setNumber`, a list with exactly one element that is a `Number` is `setNumber` of that element, anything else is shown as text (see the text rule).

Type `percentage`: Excel column style `PERCENTAGE`, printable percentage style `PERCENT_TEXT`, rounding as for `number`, header right-aligned; a number (or single-number list) is `setPercentage(value as double)` (a fraction).

Type `datetime`: the display format's `style` decides the cell. When `format-helper` reports that style as including the time of day, the Excel column style is `DATETIME` and a number is `setDatetime(new Date(value))`; otherwise style `DATE` and `setDate(new Date(value))` (value in epoch ms). The header is right-aligned; no rounding is applied.

Type `duration`: Excel column style `DURATION`, header right-aligned, a number is `setDuration(ms / 1000)`. In the printable export durations are shown as calendar time (`setDurationAsCalendarTime(true)`) unless the display format's boolean `workTime` is true.

For the four typed kinds, a value that is not a number is shown with `setText` of the display format's rendering: `number` - the user locale's number format, `percentage` - its percent format, both with exactly `rounding` decimals (clamped 0..9, 0 when absent), half-up, no grouping; `datetime` - `format-helper`'s date format for the current user and `style`; `duration` - the current user's work-time duration text when `workTime` is true, else calendar-time text. A string is first parsed (as a double for number and percentage, as a long for datetime and duration) and formatted, or shown unchanged when it does not parse. A list is shown as its non-null elements formatted the same way and joined with `, `, but shows nothing if any element is not a number or string. Booleans, item identities and maps show nothing; null shows nothing.

Type `wiki`: Excel column style `DEFAULT`; printable `setHtml` of the attribute in `html` format and a multiline column; Excel rich text of the attribute in `html` with parameter `excel` = true. Plain text (no or unknown type): Excel style `DEFAULT`, `setText` of the attribute in `text` format, printable multiline. Header left-aligned in both.

Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `notes` and no export format (both formats); null for other keys. It requests attribute `itemProperty` (format `text`) with parameter `name` = the column's `note` parameter, `notes` when absent. Each cell is `setText` of that value (null leaves it empty); the printable column is multiline.
Header text: the column's name when non-empty, otherwise i18n `s.w.notes.column-type.name` (`Notes`).
Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `timeinstatus` and no export format (both formats); null for other keys.

It requests attribute `timeinstatus` (format `duration`) whose parameters are exactly the column parameters with keys `statuses`, `useCurrentStatus`, `reopen`, `targetEnabled`, `targetStatuses` and `calendar`, values copied unchanged; every other column parameter is left out. With `aggregate` = `sum` it becomes attribute `sum` (format `duration`) with `attribute` = that and `distinct` = the column's boolean `distinct`.

Header text: the column's name, else i18n `s.w.time-in-status.column-type.name` (`Time in Status`), or for a sum `Σ Time in Status` (`sw.column.opt.aggr.sum.colname`). The header is right-aligned in Excel.

When the column's object parameter `displayFormat` has `type` = `duration`, the Excel column style is `DURATION` and cells are `setDuration(ms / 1000)`; the printable column shows calendar time unless the column's own top-level boolean parameter `workTime` is true. Otherwise (no display format or another type) the column style is `DEFAULT` and cells are `setNumber` of the attribute read in `number` format (the duration in milliseconds). Null leaves the cell empty.

Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `query-match` and no export format (both formats); null for other keys. It uses attribute `query-match` with parameters `query` and `queryType` (each only when the column has it, values unchanged).

Without a sum: the printable cell is `setHtml` of `query-match` in `html` format; the Excel cell is `setNumber` of `query-match` in `number` format (1 for a match, 0 for no match). With `aggregate` = `sum`, both formats show `setNumber` of attribute `sum` (format `number`) with `attribute` = `query-match` in `number` format and `distinct` = the column's boolean `distinct`: the count of matching rows in the sub-tree. Excel column style `DEFAULT`, header left-aligned; null leaves the cell empty.

Header text: the column's name when non-empty; otherwise the trimmed `query` when it is 1 to 40 characters long; otherwise (empty or longer) i18n `s.w.query-match.column-type.name` (`Query match`) when there is no `queryType`, else `s.w.query-match.column.+<queryType>+.name` (`jql` gives `JQL query`, `sjql` `S-JQL query`, `text` `Text query`). For a sum column that default is wrapped as `Σ {0}` (`sw.column.opt.aggr.sum.colname`).

Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `comment` and no export format (both formats); null for other keys. It shows attribute `comment` (format `html`, no parameters): printable `setHtml` in a multiline column; Excel rich text of `comment` in `html` with parameter `excel` = true. Null leaves the cell empty.
Header text: the column's name, or i18n `s.w.lastcomment.column-type.name` (`Last Comment`).

Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `tempo-worklogged` and no export format. It handles the column only when `tempo-integration` reports Tempo Timesheets available (installed, enabled and the current user has timesheets access); otherwise, and for other column keys, it returns null and the column is not exported.

It requests attribute `tempo-worklogged` (format `duration`) with parameters `accounts` (list of longs), `users` (list of strings), `teams` (list of longs), each an empty list when the column has none, `billable` (boolean, false when absent), and `dateFrom`, `dateTo` (unchanged). When `dateFrom` or `dateTo` is missing it returns null.

With `aggregate` = `sum` it uses attribute `sum` (format `duration`) over that attribute with the column's boolean `distinct`. Header: the column's name, else i18n `sw.column.tempo-worklogged.name` (`Tempo Work Logged`), for a sum `Σ Tempo Work Logged`. Cells are `setDuration(ms / 1000)`, column style `DURATION`, header right-aligned, in both formats.

Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `tempo-timeplanned` and no export format. It handles the column only when `tempo-integration` reports the Tempo planning API available (plugin installed, enabled and the current user has planner access); otherwise, and for other keys, it returns null.

It requests attribute `tempo-timeplanned` (format `duration`) with parameters `users` (list of strings), `teams` and `roles` (lists of longs), each an empty list when absent, and `dateFrom`, `dateTo` (unchanged). When `dateFrom` or `dateTo` is missing it returns null.

With `aggregate` = `sum` it uses attribute `sum` (format `duration`) over that attribute with the column's boolean `distinct`. Header: the column's name, else i18n `sw.column.tempo-timeplanned.name` (`Tempo Planned Time`), for a sum `Σ Tempo Planned Time`. Cells are `setDuration(ms / 1000)`, column style `DURATION`, header right-aligned, in both formats.

Declared as a `structure-performance-log-provider`. Each time the log is built it returns a branch `Jira instance information` with exactly four leaves in this order: the Structure plugin's version (the plugin `com.almworks.jira.structure`'s `PluginInformation.getVersion()`, read once and then reused), `JIRA: <version>` (Jira's `BuildUtilsInfo.getVersion()`), the cluster line, and the current server-local time as `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss`. No other child is ever added.

The cluster line is `cluster: on, node: <node id>` when Jira's `ClusterInfo.isClustered()` is true (node id from `ClusterInfo.getNodeId()`), otherwise `cluster: off`. Both answers are read once per plugin start and reused.

Declared as a `structure-performance-log-provider`. It returns a branch `Structures` with one node per structure the current user may administer, as `structure-manager` lists all structures at `PermissionLevel.ADMIN` (non-archived, in its name order); with no such structure the result is null. Each node is titled `<name>[<id>] (owner:<owner user key>)` and is present even when it has no children.
Under each structure, in this order and each only when non-empty: `Synchronizers`, `Generators`, `Effectors`, and the manual-adjustments node.

`Synchronizers` lists the structure's installed synchronizers as `sync-observer` reports them, each titled `<sync id> ; <module key> ; <parameters as text> ; <user key>; enabled` or `...; disabled` (note: no space before the last semicolon) according to `sync-observer`'s enabled answer.

For a synchronizer with module key `com.almworks.jira.structure:sync-filter` whose parameters are a map: when `filterId` > 0, the saved filter with that id and every saved filter it references are listed under the synchronizer's node; otherwise when `jql` is non-blank, the saved filters that JQL references. The node is then a branch of those filter leaves; without any it stays a leaf.

Saved filters referenced by a JQL are found by parsing it with Jira's `JqlQueryParser` and following `filter` clauses through AND, OR and NOT (not WAS or CHANGED clauses, not function operands). A string operand is trimmed, lower-cased and looked up with `SearchRequestManager.findByNameIgnoreCase`; a number operand with `getSearchRequestById`. Each found filter is included and its own query is followed the same way (each filter is fetched at most once per log build). Each leaf is `<id> ; <name> ; <query string>`; their order is not defined. Missing filters are skipped; unparsable JQL gives no leaves and logs `Unable to parse query: <jql>` at INFO.

`Generators` lists the generator rows of the structure's own forest, in forest order (depth-first): each is `<generator id> ; <module key> ; <parameters map as text> ; ancestorRows=[<ancestor row ids from the top down, comma-space separated>]` (`[]` for a top-level generator). When the generator's parameters have a non-blank `jql`, the node becomes a branch of the saved filters that JQL references.

`Effectors` lists the rows of item type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-effector` the same way, with the effector instance's id, module key and parameters (and the saved filters of a non-blank `jql` parameter).

When a generator or effector row cannot be read or its generator or effector is not found (`MissingRowException` or `StructureException`), its entry is the leaf `0 ; error=<exception text>` (the id shown is 0). When the structure's forest cannot be read (`StructureException`) no generators or effectors are listed. When the ancestor path cannot be determined it is shown as `[-1]`.

The manual-adjustments node is titled `Manual adjustments [ON]` or `Manual adjustments [OFF]` (the per-structure setting) when manual adjustments are enabled globally, otherwise `Manual adjustments [OFF] (structure: [ON|OFF], dark feature: [OFF])`. Its leaves are the structure's adjustments, each as the compact JSON of its stored form; with no adjustments the node is omitted.

If building one synchronizer, generator, effector or adjustment entry throws an `Exception` or `LinkageError`, that entry becomes the leaf `Unexpected exception occurred. See logs for more information.` (logged at error level) and the other entries are still listed.

Declared as a `structure-performance-log-provider`. It visits every saved Jira filter (`SearchRequestManager.visitAll`, no permission filtering) and returns a branch `Saved filters with structure()` with one leaf `<id> ; <name> ; <jql>` per filter whose JQL text uses the structure function, in visiting order; with none the result is null.

A JQL uses the structure function when its text, ignoring case, contains the word `structure` starting at a word boundary, followed by optional whitespace and `(`: `issue in structure(1)` and `issue in STRUCTURE ("a")` match; `mystructure(` and `structures(` do not; a null query does not. It is a text match, so the pattern inside a quoted string also matches.

Declared as a `structure-performance-log-provider`. It returns a branch `Attribute System` whose children are, in order, the last cache-cleanup record of `attribute-performance-tracker` (when there is one) and then its slow requests oldest first. With neither, the result is null.

Each record is a branch titled `<total time>ms; <start>; <name>` (total time in whole ms, start formatted `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss,SSS` in the record's own time zone, e.g. `812ms; 2026-10-29 10:15:02,123; cacheCleanup`). Its children are first one leaf `<counter>: <value>` per counter, the value printed as a Java double (e.g. `removed: 12.0`), then the nested steps (the up-to-5 slowest the tracker kept) as nodes of the same form, recursively.

A record (or nested step) with no counters and no nested steps yields no node and is silently left out. If every record is like that, the `Attribute System` branch is still returned but has no children (as the original does).

Declared as a `structure-performance-log-provider`. It reports the state of the item change tracker that `item-tracker` uses, chosen once when this provider is created. On a single-node server, or on Data Center with dark feature `structure.delegatingItemTracker.enableAsyncEventsQueue` set to false, that tracker has nothing to report and the log is null.

On Data Center with the asynchronous event queue (the default), the log is a branch with a fixed title naming that tracker with four leaves in order: `node: <cluster node id>` (`?` while the node id has not been read yet), `signature: <node signature in octal>` (0 before one is assigned), `threadCount: <number of event-writer threads started so far>`, `queueSize: <events received but not yet written>` (-1 when the two versions are not comparable).
